title: How Jim Knowles made Tennessee's defense CFP-caliber almost overnight - CBS Sports
description: In his first season as defensive coordinator, Knowles' unit has Vols fans dreaming big
body:
In his first season as defensive coordinator, Knowles' unit has Vols fans dreaming big
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When Tennessee hired Jim Knowles as its defensive coordinator, conventional wisdom held that the Volunteers would need to be patient. It typically takes Knowles' scheme a couple of years to really take effect.Over seven weeks, Tennessee's defense looks as if Knowles has been with the program for a decade.In Saturday afternoon's 26-10 win, the Volunteers held No. 6 Alabama to 201 total yards. Keelon Russell threw for just 147 yards and committed three turnovers. The Crimson Tide went 2-for-12 on third down, and they converted just one of their three fourth-down attempts.Tennessee's defensive front was disruptive early and often, and the secondary maintained tight coverage on the Alabama receivers with Ryan Coleman-Williams out of the lineup. That combination produced five sacks and 10 tackles for loss.
Entering the day, the Volunteers were the 19th-ranked scoring defense nationally and ranked 25th in yards per game at 293.7, an improvement from 396.9 last year.The underlying metrics were just as good, with the Vols at 21st in EPA per play (-0.08). Tennessee was 105th in that category last fall at 0.12. It's a huge jump that has propelled the Volunteers forward against even the toughest opponents.Not only has Knowles' impact on Tennessee been felt immediately, but the defense is a big reason why the Volunteers find themselves at 6-1 with eyes on the College Football Playoff. A shaky offensive line and mistakes from young quarterbacks have limited the Vols' typically explosive offense, but it's rarely mattered because of what Knowles has done on the other side of the ball.
Thanks to impact transfers and assistant coaches who understand Knowles' defense, Tennessee has an elite unit it can lean on for the rest of the season.Penn State transplants leading the wayPart of this immediate success must be attributed to the players and coaches who followed Knowles from Penn State in the offseason.Starting on the field, defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam, linebacker Amare Campbell and safety Dejuan Lane have given the Vols impact players at every level of the defense. They all played a key role in the Vols' victory over Alabama.
Gilliam is one of the best defensive tackles in the country, and he was disruptive at the line of scrimmage once again. Campbell was flying around the field and picked up two tackles for loss. Lane recorded an interception and got into the backfield for 1.5 tackles for loss.Those players were already familiar with what Knowles wants to do on defense, and that has helped the rest of the personnel pick up the scheme quickly. It certainly helps that the Tennessee defensive coordinator brought a host of assistants with him from Happy Valley.LEOs coach Andrew Jackson and secondary coach Anthony Poindexter were both at Penn State last season, and Poindexter has admitted he has a better grasp of the defense in his second year teaching it, which has allowed him to relay that knowledge to the players more effectively.
Add all of that to the talent Tennessee already had on its roster or added from the transfer portal -- Tyree Weathersby, Arion Carter, Ty Redmond, Qua Moss and TJ Metcald -- and that's a recipe for immediate success.Lock down on third downAnother big improvement Tennessee has made with Knowles leading the defense comes on critical downs. Last year, the Volunteers were horrid when there was an opportunity to get off the field.Tennessee allowed opponents to convert on 43.2% of their third-down attempts, which ranked 99th nationally. That wore out the personnel and kept a high-powered offense on the sideline.
This year, the Volunteers can get off the field much more quickly. Coming into the Alabama game, the Vols allowed opponents to convert on third down at 34.92%, which ranked 44th in the country.That number will only go down after Saturday's impressive effort. Alabama converted 16.7% of its third-down attempts, and Tennessee stemmed the Tide on two of its three fourth-down attempts.Whether it was the defensive line getting into the backfield or the secondary blanketing the Alabama receivers, Tennessee refused to let Alabama extend drives. That went a long way toward the Vols controlling time of possession (35:44) and leaning on the Crimson Tide late.

schema.headline: How Jim Knowles made Tennessee's defense CFP-caliber almost overnight - CBS Sports

title: Where to watch Cowboys vs. Packers: TV, live streaming, odds, prediction for 'SNF' - CBS Sports
description: The last time these two teams met in Week 4 of the 2025 season, they combined for the highest-scoring tie in the
body:
The last time these two teams met in Week 4 of the 2025 season, they combined for the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        One of the NFL's highest-scoring rivalries will be renewed on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6 when the Green Bay Packers (3-2) host the Dallas Cowboys (2-3) at Lambeau Field on Sunday night.Last season, the Packers traveled down to Texas to face the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium, and the two teams tied at 40-40, the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era, since 1996, per CBS Sports Research. The game featured seven lead changes, including six consecutive touchdown drives with a lead change in the second half. However, this rivalry hasn't exactly been very competitive in terms of the games' final outcomes, with the Cowboys seeking their first win against the Packers since the 2016 regular season, quarterback Dak Prescott's rookie year. Since that game, Dallas is 0-5-1 in the last six games against Green Bay despite scoring 31 points per game in that stretch. The problem is their defense has allowed a combined 37 points per game during the six-game winless streak against the Packers. That's the most points per game scored by a team's offense during a six-game winless span against an opponent in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research. Sunday will mark Packers quarterback Jordan Love's first home start against the Cowboys, with both of his games against Dallas coming on the road -- a 48-32 wild card round win in the 2023 season and the 40-40 tie last year. It will also mark a homecoming for two former Packers who are now Cowboys: three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Kenny Clark and Pro Bowl edge rusher Rashan Gary. 
Let's dig into this primetime fight against two of the NFL's most historic franchises, but first, here's how you can watch:  Where to watch Cowboys vs. PackersDate: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETLocation: Lambeau Field (Green Bay, Wisconsin)TV: NBC | Stream: Fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Packers -1.5, O/U 53.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook)Cowboys vs. Packers need to knowCowboys looking to fix bad vibes on defense: In Week 5, Dallas lost a home game 24-16 on "Thursday Night Football" to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, a team it was favored by 9.5 points. Tampa Bay was starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, making his second career start in place of an injured Baker Mayfield, and Dallas allowed the Buccaneers to control the game with 241 rushing yards. That was the most for the Buccaneers in a game since the 2024 season. 
This week, there has been speculation from owner and general manager Jerry Jones about first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker moving upstairs to the booth, but Parker and head coach Brian Schottenheimer maintained he will remain on the sideline. Dallas' performance improvement plan has begun with the hiring of former Cleveland Browns coach Mike Pettine as a senior assistant. Pettine actually gave Parker his first job in the NFL when he was Green Bay's defensive coordinator in 2019. Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked defense (395.4 total yards allowed per game), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game), and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it.How fixable are the issues? "Very fixable because they're under our control," Parker said. "Very fixable."Cowboys All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams agrees. "Just from the aspect of the things that we can control are the things that we're messing up on. Effort. Playing with our technique. Playing better, things like that. Those are things we can control as a unit, we can control as a unit. It's fixable. We just have to make our best effort to fix those things. 
Packers' Jordan Love aims to maintain an explosive passing game to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden: Packers quarterback Jordan Love is fresh off his best game of 2026 in Week 5, a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, which makes him the Packers' record holder for the most passing yards in a game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He beat the previous record of 345 yards passing by Lynn Dickey, set back in 1983. The victory, 24 points, ranks as the largest win against the Bears since 2014, the year Rodgers won the second of his four NFL MVPs. The Packers are now 5-3 against the Bears in Love's eight career starts against them since 2023, including playoffs. "We were flowing today. Executed at a really high level. I was proud of everybody. That's what it looks like when we play to our standard, and we got playmakers making plays down the field, O-line doing a great job," Love said postgame on FOX. "That's the standard for us. ... This is huge. This is a win we needed at home, getting us rolling and keep building off this."
Love went big-game hunting with regularity to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches), making Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016. It last occurred when Davante Adams and Jordy Nelson accomplished the feat against the Tennessee Titans 10 years ago. Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards.In total, Love connected on six of eight of his eight throws of 20-plus air yards for a career-high 258 yards and 2 touchdowns on his passes of 20-plus air yards. Per the league's Next Gen stats, only Russell Wilson (264 with the New York Giants in Week 2 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys) had more in the NGS era (since 2016). According to ESPN Insights, Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006. Slowing this high-flying passing attack down will be a tall task for a struggling Cowboys defense. 
A stoppable force vs. a movable object: The Packers rank dead last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (60.4) and third-down offense (27.6% conversion rate) thanks to missing running back Josh Jacobs while he was on the commissioner's exempt list and dealing with some offensive line injuries. Across from them on the line of scrimmage at Lambeau Field on Sunday will be the Cowboys' last-ranked run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and last-ranked third-down defense (52.6% conversion rate allowed). Whichever team can find an edge here will likely emerge victorious.New Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr. primed to return in primetime: New Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was set to play his first full game as a Cowboy in Week 5 before a stomach bug made him a late scratch hours before kickoff. However, Porter Jr. is now recovered from his illness and aims to play a full starter's load of snaps. He played on 48.1% (25 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in their 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans in Week 4 just days after being acquired in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier that week. He is officially listed as questionable to play on Sunday with an ankle injury, but on Wednesday he said he is "definitely" ready to be a full-time starter for Dallas. Parker agreed, saying the team is ready for him to have a "heavily increased" workload against the Packers.Cowboys vs. Packers predictionDespite Porter Jr. likely returning to action for Dallas in Week 6, their defense won't be able to stifle Love, Watson and Golden through the air. Whichever receiver between Watson and Golden that cornerback DaRon Bland, who has struggled with his footing on the field of late, will break free for big gains on a consistent basis. Yes, the Cowboys do have the NFL's No. 7 scoring offense (27.6 points per game) powered by Prescott, wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, wide receiver George Pickens and running back Javonte Williams. 
However, Dallas' defense struggles will limit their offense's ability to find a rhythm. The Cowboys are averaging 3.07 points per drive, the second-highest by a team under .500 through five games this century per CBS Sports Research, but their 45 drives this season are the second fewest in the league this season. Among the NFL teams that have played in all five weeks of the 2026 season, Dallas' 45 drives stand as the fewest. That's what happens when you have the league's worst run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed).That unit will struggle again in Green Bay on Sunday night as the Cowboys have yet to overcome their decision to trade All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Packers at the start of the 2025 season. Parsons won't suit up for Green Bay on Sunday night while he continues to recover from the torn ACL he suffered at the end of last season, but his presence will continue to haunt Dallas' narrative.  Pick: Packers 34, Cowboys 24

title: Knicks finalize roster as James Wiseman gets last spot over Bruce Brown - CBS Sports
description: Wiseman, a former No. 2 overall pick, will provide frontcourt depth for the reigning NBA champs
body:
Wiseman, a former No. 2 overall pick, will provide frontcourt depth for the reigning NBA champs
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New York Knicks finalized their roster heading into the 2026-27 season on Saturday, waiving veteran Bruce Brown in order to retain former No. 2 overall pick James Wiseman on the regular season roster. Wiseman has been featured regularly in the Knicks preseason games, averaging 8.0 points and 4.3 rebounds in four appearances in the preseason. After seeing Mitchell Robinson walk in free agency to the rival Boston Celtics, New York needed to bolster its center rotation behind Karl-Anthony Towns. The Knicks signed Andre Drummond in free agency to be their new backup, but needed additional depth and brought in Wiseman on an Exhibit 9 deal (training camp contract), which they'll now convert into a league minimum deal that gets Wiseman back onto a roster with a chance to contribute for the first time in a few years. 
Wiseman played in just five games the last two seasons in Indiana, and while he'll be reserve depth in New York, he could see some regular-season action as they look to be mindful of minutes coming off of a championship run. 
The former No. 2 pick of the Warriors has not been a regular rotation player since 2023-24 in Detroit, when he averaged 7.1 points and 5.3 rebounds per game in 63 appearances. Wiseman was part of the Warriors' initial plans to try and build for the future while competing in the present, but he struggled to produce at a high level and has had defensive woes since entering the league. The Knicks will hope he can provide some size in reserve when called upon for spot duty this season after impressing Mike Brown enough in the preseason to keep him on the roster. 
For Brown, he'll hope to find an opportunity elsewhere after being waived. Brown played in all 82 games a season ago with the Denver Nuggets, averaging 7.9 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game.

title: NFL Week 6 player props, anytime TD best bets: Jaylen Warren, Woody Marks top picks - CBS Sports
description: Woody Marks steps into the spotlight in London and Jaylen Warren stays hot among five smart plus-money end zone p
body:
Woody Marks steps into the spotlight in London and Jaylen Warren stays hot among five smart plus-money end zone picks
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Sunday around the NFL, the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, the Baltimore Ravens and Cleveland Browns will fight for the AFC North lead, while the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers face off under the lights in Lambeau Field. Get ready for another wild week. Let's discuss some anytime touchdown bets. These have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Last week, we hit on our headliner in Trey McBride (+115), and Christian McCaffrey -- who was shockingly listed at -130. Let's see what we have cooking up for Week 6. Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider. These will not be predictable choices like a Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a running back in London. 1. Texans RB Woody Marks (+110)With David Montgomery ruled out due to a groin injury, Woody Marks is going to be the Texans' lead back in London against the Jaguars. He's actually Houston's leading rusher this season with 149 yards, despite Montgomery having registered nine more rushes. Marks has found the end zone twice over the last three games, and saw an uptick in usage in the passing game last week against the Tennessee Titans. This is a massive game for the Texans, who are looking to find a rhythm following their slow start and make up ground in the AFC South. I like Marks to score. 
2. Steelers RB Jaylen Warren (+110)Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren has been on fire. Last Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts, he racked up 188 total yards and two touchdowns -- becoming the first player since Herschel Walker in 1986 to score a 50-yard rushing touchdown and an 80-yard receiving touchdown in the same game. Warren has actually recorded the second-most scrimmage yards (640) through five games in Steelers history, behind Le'Veon Bell in 2014, and has the third-most scrimmage yards in the NFL despite receiving the 17th-most touches (89). He's been a beast, and the Steelers' best weapon on offense. 3. Titans RB Tony Pollard (+145)The Titans are a disaster, but I think they could keep things close with the Colts this week. If they can't, then that's a massive problem. The Colts rank bottom six in total defense, passing defense, rushing defense, scoring defense and yards per play. 
Tony Pollard has found the end zone just once this season, but he's still one of the Titans' main vehicles on offense. I also think he's a bit underrated. Pollard is one of just two NFL players to record 1,000 rushing yards in each of the last four seasons. The other player? Derrick Henry. 4. Colts TE Tyler Warren (+145)Speaking of that Titans-Colts game, tight end Tyler Warren could be in line for a big outing. He caught seven of nine targets for a season-high 83 yards last week against the Steelers, and also rushed for a touchdown. Warren has two of the Colts' three receiving touchdowns on the season, and he's Indy's most important weapon behind Jonathan Taylor. 5. Bills TE Dalton Kincaid (+170)It looked like Dalton Kincaid was going to be a pillar in Joe Brady's revamped offense, but the Buffalo Bills tight end has recorded seven yards receiving in each of the last two weeks. He was averaging 112.5 receiving yards per game through two weeks! I'm going to take him to bounce back and find the end zone against a Las Vegas Raiders defense that has been diced up by tight ends before. In Week 3 against the New Orleans Saints, the Raiders allowed a whopping FOUR touchdowns to tight ends. 
Buffalo's Monday night victory over the Los Angeles Rams was a little weird. Josh Allen threw for just 210 yards. I think the Bills' passing attack at large has a better outing against Vegas. Bonus. Texans WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (+475)Could you imagine if Marvin Harrison Jr. shows up and catches a touchdown in his first game with the Texans after being traded away by the Arizona Cardinals? I'm not telling you to bet on it, but here's the line if you were curious!

title: The Spurs will start Dylan Harper on opening night, so where does that leave De'Aaron Fox? - CBS Sports
description: The Spurs will try out a three-guard lineup again at the start of this season with Harper, Fox and Stephon Castle
body:
The Spurs will try out a three-guard lineup again at the start of this season with Harper, Fox and Stephon Castle
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For opening night, at least, the San Antonio Spurs have answered the single biggest starting lineup question of the 2026-27 season. Dylan Harper, the No. 2 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft and the second-best player in San Antonio's NBA Finals loss to the New York Knicks, will officially join the starting five alongside Victor Wembanyama, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell... and De'Aaron Fox, the expensive veteran whose injured ankle and ensuing struggles loomed large over that Finals defeat.San Antonio barely used the three-guard lineup last season, and for good reason. It was outscored significantly in both 54-possession regular-season and 83-possession postseason samples last year. The lineup outscored the Phoenix Suns by 10 points in 25 possessions in a recent preseason victory, but the Spurs shot just 2 of 9 on 3s when all three guards played together in that game.That is the primary concern here. Harper, Fox and Castle are all strong drivers with questionable 3-point shots. Such players typically do best when surrounded by other shooters. The Spurs can get away with having two of them on the floor at once because their center, Victor Wembanyama, is game-breaking in dozens of ways, including his ability to space the floor. San Antonio took off last season when it upgraded its shooting by inserting Julian Champagnie into the starting lineup.With all three guards playing together, though, the delicate balance between shooting and ball-handling has tilted too far toward the latter. Ball-handling doesn't have nearly the amplifying effect that shooting does, and opponents will inevitably cheat off of the two guards without the ball in their hands whenever one of them is trying to create shots with it. The trio is so talented, and comes with the inherent advantage of playing with Wembanyama, that the Spurs will almost certainly win most of the games it plays with this starting lineup. 

        
            
                Ranking the NBA's top 100 players: Victor Wembanyama enters 2026-27 season at No. 1
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
But it's certainly suboptimal. We all know where this is probably heading. Harper was simply too good to keep coming off of the bench, and Castle is too good to ever move there. Eventually, the best version of the Spurs likely has Fox, the oldest and most expensive of the three guards, coming off of the bench as Harper did a season ago. San Antonio's starters with Champagnie playing alongside two of the guards outscored opponents by 17.6 points per 100 possessions a season ago. The formula of two guards, two shooters and Wembanyama is this team's endgame.Yet even if that's the case, the Spurs are slow-playing this. In the long run, that's probably the sensible approach. Benching a reigning All-Star on a max contract is fraught. Fox very intentionally steered himself to San Antonio through a direct trade request, presumably expecting to be the starting point guard on a dynasty. Players of his stature and age are rarely eager to come off of the bench. Asking him to do so on opening night based off of a poor Finals series in which he was injured risks alienating a key player and, cynically, destroying what little trade value he might have left.Even if the Spurs do plan to bench Fox down the line, easing him into it seems like the safest approach. He still has a chance to prove that this three-guard lineup can work, and if it does, well, maybe there's less of a problem here than we're assuming. If it proves uncomfortable or if the lineup data suggests it's flopping, the Spurs at least have empirical data supporting a change. They can at least tell Fox that they tried.
They'd hardly be the first team to try this approach to benching a star. Russell Westbrook went through it with both Los Angeles teams, for instance. The Lakers benched him after an 0-3 start in the 2022-23 season. The Clippers let him and James Harden start five games together a year later, lost all five, and then went 27-7 in their next 34 after benching him. Sometimes, you have to sacrifice a few games for the greater good. Players of this caliber tend to expect a certain degree of respect that the attempt at least affords.The notion of sacrificing games is going to be a bitter pill to swallow in this case, specifically, because San Antonio's competition for the No. 1 seed in the Western Conference practically never does so. The Oklahoma City Thunder churn out 60-win seasons in their sleep, and home-court advantage in the practically preordained Western Conference Finals between them, despite San Antonio's road victory a year ago, is meaningful. But that same road victory showed the Spurs that what matters isn't October or November. It's May and June. If the Spurs have to take the long road to optimized lineups and locker room harmony, so be it. For now, they're giving Harper the starting job he so clearly deserves and tabling the Fox end of the equation until the issue is forced.

        The New England Patriots offense will get a major boost this week. The team announced it activated star wide receiver A.J. Brown off injured reserve to play against the New York Jets on Sunday.Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 and has missed four weeks so far, the minimum required when a team places any player on IR. The three-time Pro Bowler returned to practice this week, but was limited all three days. His official game designation is questionable. The WR had just three receptions on four targets for 26 yards before going down against the Seattle Seahawks in the Super Bowl rematch season opener.The Patriots offense was rocky to start the season, with quarterback Drake Maye struggling with forcing passes and committing turnovers. Their biggest offensive struggle came against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3, as they failed to get into the end zone and lost 35-6.
Without Brown, the worry was that the Patriots couldn't march down the field without a true WR1. Maye's capabilities were called into question, with many wondering whether last year's near-MVP season was a fluke.Despite his absence, the Maye and Co. have seemed to get it together and have increased production tenfold. They look like a team to beat over the last two weeks, having defeated the Buffalo Bills 29-26 and the Las Vegas Raiders 45-17. The Patriots are currently 10th in passing yards (1,274), but tied for most interceptions (7).Brown returning should elevate the offense, finally give fans a look at what a Maye-Brown offense looks like, and continue the upward trajectory. 
If Brown does not return this week against the Jets, he could return in Week 7 against the Chicago Bears.

title: Michigan benches QB Bryce Underwood to start second half vs. Penn State - CBS Sports
description: Kyle Whittingham sat Underwood, a former five-star recruit, after a scoreless first half against Penn State on Sa

Kyle Whittingham sat Underwood, a former five-star recruit, after a scoreless first half against Penn State on Saturday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:02 pm ET

        Pressed to bench Bryce Underwood as Michigan's starting quarterback throughout this season, Kyle Whittingham finally made the call to sit him to start the second half of Saturday's game against Penn State.After failing to score over the first two quarters with countless empty possessions dictated by faulty execution, two interceptions and several short-armed throws from the five-star sophomore, Michigan went to the bench in favor of freshman Tommy Carr.The Wolverines scored their first points on Carr's second possession thanks to Bryson Kuzdzal's 43-yard touchdown run after Penn State lost containment on the outside. Earlier this week, Michigan offensive coordinator Jason Beck addressed Underwood and the expectations upon the former No. 1 QB recruit.
"Nothing's ever good enough, let alone when it's not going great, right? You always want to play better," Beck said. "There are always things to improve, there are always things to do better. The thing I'll say with Bryce is he cares, and he works hard. It matters to him, and he's feeling that outside noise and all that as much as anybody. He's really handling that well with his approach and the teammate he is, so we're always working to get better and improve."Carr, a former four-star signee and the grandson of former Wolverines coach Lloyd Carr, appeared in only one game previously this season, completing both passes he threw against UTEP.
Carr's older brother is Heisman Trophy candidate and Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr.

title: Steve Sarkisian buyout, contract details as Texas football coach - CBS Sports
description: A second straight loss to an unranked opponent has the temperature rising in Austin
body:
A second straight loss to an unranked opponent has the temperature rising in Austin
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:14 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Texas Longhorns made some unfortunate history on Saturday, becoming the first program since 1961 to be ranked No. 1 in the AP poll and then lose back-to-back games to unranked opponents. After blowing a lead in the Red River Rivalry against Oklahoma, Texas jumped out to another big first-half lead against Florida on Saturday before the Gators, led by backup quarterback Tramell Jones, mounted a comeback for a win in Austin that has the temperature rising under Steve Sarkisian. Sark was brought into Texas to do two things. The first was to raise the floor and make them a consistently good football team. That he's accomplished, going 35-8 in his last three seasons. The second thing he was supposed to do once he raised the floor was to turn Texas into a perennial title contender. That has yet to happen despite being ranked No. 1 in the AP poll at different points in each of the last two seasons, and the Longhorns once again appear headed towards a year outside the nation's elite tier at 4-2. There is a question of whether Sarkisian is the coach to get Texas to that final step needed to win their first national title in 20 years, but if Texas were interested in making a change, it'd cost the Longhorns boosters an awful lot of money. 
Steve Sarkisian buyout, contract details Sarkisian received a new contract in 2025 that extended his tenure through 2031 and raised his salary to one of the highest in college football. Including this season, Sarkisian's contract is for six more years and just over $70 million. His buyout calls for him to be paid 85% of his remaining contract balance, which would mean Texas would be on the hook for $50.15 million after the conclusion of the 2026 season. That wouldn't be the biggest contract buyout in history -- or even the state of Texas -- but it would still be in the top five of the biggest buyouts ever. To pay that much, it would require Texas to not just be frustrated with Sarkisian, but to be completely convinced he can't get the Longhorns to the pinnacle of the sport. Texas would also have to be certain they have a better coach lined up, and while they have the resources to tempt any coach in the country, there isn't an obvious choice for the Longhorns. 
As of now, two losses don't doom Texas from being a College Football Playoff team. Given their win over Ohio State, they could very well become the first team to make it with three losses, but if Sarkisian's Longhorns were to miss the playoff entirely, given where they were after Week 5, perhaps the chatter that exists mostly in frustration online could turn into a real exploration of their options in Austin.

title: Bears expected to start Caleb Williams vs. Falcons, per report - CBS Sports
description: The Chicago Bears are likely getting their No. 1 pick back this week
body:
The Chicago Bears are likely getting their No. 1 pick back this week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Chicago Bears are planning to start quarterback Caleb Williams on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons, according to multiple reports. Williams missed three games due to a torn hamstring and this week was able to return to practice at full capacity and took the starter's reps. He is officially listed as questionable for their Week 6 game, but a full week of practice showed he was trending in the right direction.Before going down with his injury, Williams played in two games: a 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers and a 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, the game where he suffered the torn hamstring. He had a 65.6 completion percentage, 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in his two appearances.Williams reposted a compilation video on TikTok earlier on Saturday that had many believing he was celebrating his return. The video starts with a compilation of criticisms of how he reacted to his injury, followed by a message from a fictional character from the Chicago-based show "The Bear," who says, "I think that flicked a switch in me where I was like, f--- you. Watch this." The video then goes into highlights of Williams playing. 
The 24-year-old has openly criticized how people have reacted to his injury. When he was carted off, Williams gave a thumbs-up and raised his fist, which, to many, made it seem like the injury was very severe. Shortly after, there were reports that Williams may not miss a game.Williams feels his "character has been attacked" and said to the media this week, "It was a hamstring tear and a pretty serious one. We got a grade, but I wouldn't say it's deserved to be put out there after all the false ones. So next question."In his absence, the Bears have leaned on Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum, who were able to record two wins of the three games without their starter. Chicago is coming off a 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers. 
In Week 5's loss, head coach Ben Johnson benched Bagent for Keenum after Bagent went 12-of-21 with 87 yards, two picks and no touchdowns. Keenum didn't fare much better, going 11-of-19 with 108 yards, one interception and no touchdowns. Getting Williams back should be a big boost for the Bears offense, as they sit at 3-2 in a difficult division where the race is close and the top team, the Vikings, have yet to lose. Williams was drafted as the top pick in the 2024 draft and helped lead the team to the playoffs in his second season with the team. He did not miss a game in his first two seasons.

title: Auburn takes down Georgia: Tigers score massive upset over No. 1 Bulldogs - CBS Sports
description: Alex Golesh earned a signature win in Year 1 -- the Tigers' first over a ranked foe since 2021
body:
Alex Golesh earned a signature win in Year 1 -- the Tigers' first over a ranked foe since 2021
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:23 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Georgia picked a bad time to play its worst game of the season on Saturday afternoon against Auburn. The Bulldogs allowed a blocked field goal, turned it over three times and committed a couple of critical penalties contributing directly to the Tigers' stunning 27-24 victory. The Auburn win snaps Georgia's 54-game winning streak against unranked competition. Georgia committed three personal fouls against Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown, including one in the final seconds that put the Tigers in position for Alex McPherson's game-winning field goal as time expired.Smart said before the game he was worried about Auburn's physicality and his team being banged up coming off last week's win at Alabama, and it showed as the Tigers borrowed from the Bulldogs' playbook by winning at the line of scrimmage.
Georgia led 14-0 before Auburn scored the game's next 24 points to take a 24-14 lead into the fourth quarter. The Tigers' victory was their first over a ranked opponent since 2021 and marked their first win over a top-ranked foe since doing it twice during the 2017 campaign.On a critical 3rd-and-11 with 1:16 to play at its own 29-yard line, Auburn had a bad snap, resulting in an immediate punt and giving Georgia a potential game-winning possession. However, Stockton lost a fumble near midfield with 58 seconds left to put the Tigers in business with all three timeouts.Georgia had won nine straight against Auburn dating back to 2017 and it was only Smart's second rivalry loss against the Tigers in 12 tries.
Auburn's a team of believersGeorgia was previously 41-4 when ranked No. 1 under Smart, including an 18-0 at home. A teary-eyed Auburn coach Alex Golesh tried to put words with his emotions after his first signature win for the Tigers in his first season as the leader of the program."(Golesh's son) Bear said Thursday, 'Dad, can I get on the field after we win' … you're on the field bro,," Golesh said. "I'm just grateful for our guys. You can have so many narratives and stories … I'm just grateful for our guys, our coaches, our fan base … it's been through a lot. We're going to build Auburn back to where everybody wants it. One game at a time. Just hang with us."
Golesh said he received texts before the game from Auburn legends Takeo Spikes and Jason Campbell, among others, reminding him that he is the right man for the job.No Xavier Atkins, no problem for Tigers Auburn suspended their top defensive player, Xavier Atkins, for Saturday's game, but managed to put together one of its most complete performances of the season on that side of the football.  Stockton had a couple chunk completion midway through the fourth quarter on Georgia's second-to-last possession, but that was the only time since the first quarter the Tigers failed to dictate the game's tempo.
After trailing by two touchdowns early, Auburn's defense came up with stop after stop to help build a 10-point lead in the second half. The Tigers held Georgia to 113 yards rushing on 28 total carries, including a 2.1 average from Nate Frazier, who was making his return to the lineup."Coach (DJ) Durkin, their defensive coordinator, has been one of the best in the conference over all the years he's been in the conference," Smart said before the game. "He's a great defensive football coach. We've got a lot of links, a lot of respect for him. Our guys have to get ready to go play."Brown finished with 115 yards on the ground for Auburn, along with a 61-yard effort on 13 carries from Jeremiah Cobb. It was the ground and pound approach that worked for Golesh's team against an opponent usually dominant in the trenches.

One of college football's great rivalries takes center stage on Saturday night when No. 3 Miami welcomes Florida State for their traditional October clash

        Get ready for one of college football's most bitter rivalries when No. 3 Miami welcomes Florida State at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday  for their traditional October clash. As usual, the game has ACC and national title race implications, though this season those conversations are focused far more on the Hurricanes, who finished last season as the national runner-up and is currently the heavy favorite to win the ACC in 2026. Things are far different for Florida State and embattled coach Mike Norvell, who entered the year facing serious job pressure and now risks falling to 3-4 on the season and 1-3 in ACC play if the Seminoles cannot pull a stunning upset. Wins against Miami in 2021, 2022 and 2023 were crucial building blocks of Norvell's eventual ACC Championship run, but now it's Mario Cristobal who has the chance to string together three straight wins in the series after the Hurricanes got the better of Florida State in 2024 and 2025. The return to Miami Gardens also spotlights what has become a notable home-field advantage for Miami in this recent run, as the Hurricanes are 15-1 at home since the start of the 2024 season, including that 36-14 win against the Seminoles in Hard Rock Stadium two years ago. Miami has been absolute rock stars in the ACC and the sport as a whole, continuing the momentum from the team's College Football Playoff run with eye-popping scores and stat-stuffing performances to start the 2026 season. Florida State hopes to provide more resistance than the average Miami opponent, but even that might not be enough to stop the ACC's most potent national title contender.
Where to watch Miami vs. Florida State liveDate: Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time: 7 p.m. ETLocation: Hard Rock Stadium -- Miami Gardens, FloridaTV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  Miami vs. Florida State: Need to know  A big stage for Darian Mensah's Heisman Trophy case: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has been playing at an elite level all season, but the lopsided wins and predicted blowouts haven't given him the stage and audience that Saturday night's rivalry game will command. Miami may be in a far better place than Florida State this season, but this iconic rivalry will still bring the attention of Heisman Trophy voters to Hard Rock Stadium to see how Mensah performs under the pressure. Currently, he's one of just two FBS quarterbacks with 15-plus passing touchdowns and zero interceptions and boasts the best completion percentage (84.2%) and passer rating (212.2) in all of FBS. Mensah will still have a road trip to Notre Dame and a few other opportunities to shine in the spotlight, but Saturday night could prove to be the launching point for Mensah to push Jeremiah Smith in the Heisman conversation.   Florida State struggling against top teams: While Florida State has won three national championships and spent 72 weeks ranked No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll throughout its history, the Seminoles have struggled against the best teams in recent years. As the Seminoles take aim at their rival from the South, they do so staring down a brutal losing streak against top-3 teams from the AP poll. Florida State has lost its last eight games against AP top-three teams, last winning in the BCS National Championship Game against Auburn at the end of the 2013 season. Another losing streak that Florida State can put to bed on Saturday night is a 12-game road losing streak against teams with any AP ranking, which stretches back to a 2016 win at Miami.  
No one is beating teams like Miami is in 2026: The Hurricanes enter this annual rivalry checkpoint with one of the most dominant teams in the country, beating opponents by an average of 39.8 points per game. That's the largest points-per-game differential through five games in school history and is currently the largest among all FBS teams. Now, a skeptic would be quick to point out that a 70-point win against Florida A&M will do a lot to juice those averages, but it's the consistency with which Miami has been blitzing its opponents that stands out. Of Miami's five games, only one (a 33-20 win at Wake Forest) was decided by less than 28 points.   Miami vs. Florida State prediction, picks  Miami isn't just blowing teams out on the scoreboard this season; it's a team that's also been exceeding oddsmakers' expectations nearly every week. The Hurricanes indeed have the best point differential in FBS (+39.8), but they also rank T-14 nationally with a 4-1 record against the spread and carry the 15th-best cover margin in the country, beating the spread by an average of 7.8 points per game. With those kinds of trends, it's tough to think that Miami is a candidate for an upset alert, and Florida State's road woes make it very possible that this game will get sideways on the Seminoles. Pick: Miami -21

title: Daniel Dubois vs. Fabio Wardley 2 results: Champ retains title with quick TKO - CBS Sports
description: The Brit made it look easy in the rematch on Saturday night to maintain his status as champion
body:
The Brit made it look easy in the rematch on Saturday night to maintain his status as champion
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In May, then-WBO heavyweight champion Fabio Wardley showed incredible toughness in a losing effort against Daniel Dubois. The pair rematched on Saturday in London, and it took Dubois less than two rounds to end their rivalry, retaining the title with a second-round TKO.It took just one exchange for Dubois to deliver a big message, with a big right hand sending Wardley twisting the canvas. Wardley beat the count, showing the toughness that was fully on display in their first bout, but it was still all Dubois, landing harder, more technical punches when Wardley attempted to uncork his brand of looping power shots.Somehow, Wardley survived a furious assault from Dubois down the stretch of the opening round to make it back to his corner, but the damage was clearly done.Wardley looked hurt by every shot Dubois landed, and those shots were landing whenever Dubois decided to throw them. Rather than put their fighter through a night of damage as they had in the first meeting, Wardley's corner threw in the towel as Dubois was unloading with another flurry against the ropes in the final minute of the second round.
Many worried that Wardley had sustained potentially life-altering damage in the first bout with Dubois, though he did score two early knockdowns to keep some hope in the storm.
Coming back so quickly after taking as much damage as he had the first time was not an issue, according to Wardley, but it was clear that he and his corner both had a limited tolerance for how much damage he would take on Saturday.After former undisputed heavyweight champion Oleksandr Usyk, who holds two knockout wins over Dubois, vacated his four world championships, there are now four separate champions, and Dubois said that he looks forward to big money unification bouts in 2027.
IBF champion Filip Hrgovic entered the ring after Dubois' win to share a respectful moment, though both men expressed interest in taking part in one of those unification bouts in the near future. Dubois stopped Hrgovic in the eighth round of a 2024 bout for the interim IBF title.

title: Julian Sayin injury: Buckeyes QB to miss 'several weeks' after going down vs. Indiana - CBS Sports
description: With the veteran out, freshman backup QB Luke Fahey will likely be charged with keeping the Buckeyes' Big Ten tit
body:
With the veteran out, freshman backup QB Luke Fahey will likely be charged with keeping the Buckeyes' Big Ten title hopes and Jeremiah Smith's Heisman campaign afloat in the interim
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        No. 4 Ohio State picked up a huge 19-15 win on the road over No. 5 Indiana on Saturday, but late in the fourth quarter the Buckeyes saw quarterback Julian Sayin leave the field after taking a big hit and return wearing a sling on his right arm. After the game, Ryan Day did not provide specific details on what injury Sayin sustained, but told reporters that Sayin will be out for "several weeks." The Buckeyes offense will turn to freshman backup Luke Fahey, who was 0-for-2 passing the ball after Sayin's injury. The Buckeyes also have sophomore quarterbacks Tavien St. Clair and Kolton Stover on the roster. The win over Indiana improves Ohio State to 6-1 on the season and provides them some needed cushion in the chase for a College Football Playoff berth. The Buckeyes have a well-timed bye week next week, but then face a challenging stretch of the schedule, starting on the road against No. 19 USC on Oct. 31, before hosting Oregon and No. 25 Northwestern the following weeks. If the Buckeyes are going to contend for a national championship, they will need Sayin back in the lineup, but they will look to lean on a dominant defense and an improved rushing attack from last year to lead the way in his absence. 
Sayin missing time could also have an impact on the Heisman Trophy race as well, where Ohio State star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith was one of the frontrunners after a dominant first six weeks of the season. Smith had four catches for 68 yards and a touchdown against Indiana and now has 52 catches for 984 yards and 12 touchdowns this season, but will now need to maintain an incredible pace with a backup quarterback throwing him the ball.What are Ryan Day's options at QB?Now 6-1 with a top-five win on its resume, Ohio State has a little room for error in the race to the College Football Playoff. That said, if Sayin misses multiple games, the Buckeyes would be vulnerable against some formidable opponents.That's why Day needs to take the next couple of weeks to get a real handle on who should start against No. 19 USC on Halloween.
To this point in the season, Fahey has been the first quarterback off the bench whenever Sayin has exited the game. That may be something of a surprise, given that Fahey is a three-star freshman who wasn't exactly a heralded recruit coming out of high school in Mission Viejo, California.Fahey was the No. 38 quarterback and the No. 46 prospect out of California in the 2026 signing class, per 247Sports. Listed at 5-foot-11 and 206 pounds, Fahey isn't the biggest quarterback, but 247Sports recruiting analyst Greg Biggins had high praise for Fahey in his scouting report.
"Fahey is one of the most talented quarterbacks out West," Biggins wrote. "He's surgical from the pocket and can pick a defense a part with his accuracy and timing. Shows off a quick release, throws one of the tighter balls in the region and processes the game extremely quick. In terms of his ability to get through his progressions and reads, he's one of the more advanced signal callers in the country."
Entering Saturday's game, Fahey had appeared in three games, throwing for 203 yards and a pair of touchdowns while completing nine of his 11 passes. The kicker is that both of Fahey's incompletions resulted in interceptions.Day also has a true blue-chip prospect at his disposal in St. Clair, a five-star prospect and the No. 4 overall player in the 2025 signing class, per 247Sports.St. Clair has served as the third-string quarterback this season, and he's attempted just nine passes at the college level. The most game action he's seen at this level came in Week 1 against Ball State, when he completed 5 of 6 passes for 52 yards and a touchdown. His only pass in mop-up duty against Kent State resulted in a pick.
Despite his lack of experience, St. Clair has an impressive pedigree. St. Clair was a star at Bellefontaine High School in Ohio, and 247Sports Director of Scouting Andrew Ivins projected him as a future first-round pick with a comparison to ex-Ohio State star Justin Fields."Overall, should be viewed as a potential multi-year starter for a College Football Playoff contender that can distribute at a high level both inside and outside of the pocket after some fine-tuning," Ivins wrote. "Likely to eventually draw NFL scouts in with his build and power."Day has talent in the quarterback room, but the question is how he will split first-team reps between his two young quarterbacks over the next two weeks as he tries to determine which one is capable of leading the Buckeyes against the Trojans.
